note: Figures quoted from existing repository records. scripts/flow_report.py fails when a quote no longer appears in its source, so a figure cannot drift silently.

entries.claim: Full deterministic suite at 2.5.0: 544 tests, exit 1 with two failures and five skips. The record says both failures came from an old extracted plugin in the ignored backup directory.
entries.quote: The final full run executed 544 tests in 1081.229 seconds and returned exit 1

entries.claim: Only the two failed tests were rerun after the old directory was moved out of the checkout: both passed, exit 0, with no source change in between.
Mutation check of the shell installer tests: 30 of 34 mutants caught. The release record says why the other four were not.

1.3.0 evaluator-integrity candidate: promoted on a sealed holdout. With two blinded judges calibrated on known-good and known-bad controls, the candidate scored 8/8 in 3 of 3 paired repetitions and the baseline in 2 of 3. Three repetitions is the minimum the repository asks for a borderline promotion claim, so this is a small sample.
quote: Candidate scored 8/8 in 3/3 repetitions from both judges; baseline scored 8/8 in 2/3 from both.

entries.claim: Behavior evaluation of the 1.6.1 candidate against the 1.6.0 baseline ended in a rejected promotion. Three paired four-case response simulations scored 95/96 (baseline) and 94/96 (candidate); one sealed two-case simulation scored 15/16 and 14/16. The record says these results support no quality, token-savings or model-equivalence claim.
quote: support no quality, token-savings or model-equivalence claim

entries.claim: Scores behind the rejected promotion (baseline, candidate).
quote: 95/96; 1/3 runs pass all gates | 94/96; 1/3 runs pass all gates

entries.claim: The 2026-08-29 portfolio audit promoted three skills on a four-point structural check (0/4 to 4/4). The record calls the points literal contract assertions, not a model score.
entries.quote: The points are literal contract assertions, not a subjective model score

entries.claim: 1.6.1 response simulations: development input was 11,586 tokens per baseline call and 11,646 per candidate call. The record calls these usage receipts, not a cost comparison.
quote: Development input was 11,586 tokens per baseline call and 11,646 per candidate call
not peak context size, RAM measurements or a cost comparison

entries.claim: 1.6.1 actual execution (one local CSV repair): the receipt reports 64,216 input tokens, 48,128 of them cached, and 1,133 output tokens (473 more are listed as reasoning output), in 29.9 s.

1.6.0 smoke receipts: four single trials across two requested models reported 70,987 to 111,655 input tokens (52,480 to 90,880 cached) and 441 to 902 output tokens each. The file sets no comparison claim.
quote: "comparison_claim": "NONE; single bounded trials, different tool/context paths"

entries.claim: One recorded Codex run warned that skill descriptions were shortened to fit the skills context budget, so a host can show less than the description bytes Flow ships.
entries.quote: Skill descriptions were shortened to fit the skills context budget.

entries.claim: The 2.2.0 record: single runs do not estimate reliability.
entries.quote: Single runs do not estimate reliability.

entries.claim: The 2.3.0 record states that no runtime benchmark was run for that release and that no measured speed or token saving is claimed.
entries.quote: No measured speed or token saving is claimed.
